78693-an-artist-s-life.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “I wish you wouldn’t. I don’t want the fact to leak out that I’m not as well as I should be. Grayber in the Medical Arts Building you’ll find that this condition is not new. The museum will have no worry about their responsibility as to my health.”

arxiv-2101-04150.title: Sign-restricted matrices of 0 0 ’s, 1 1 ’s, and − 1 -1 ’s Department of Mathematics, University of Oslo, Norway. geird@math.uio.no. Corresponding author.
arxiv-2101-04150.creator: Richard A. Brualdi
arxiv-2101-04150.description: Abstract We study sign-restricted matrices (SRMs), a class of rectangular ( 0 , ± 1 ) (0,\pm 1) -matrices generalizing the alternating sign matrices (ASMs). In an SRM each partial column sum, starting from row 1, equals 0 or 1, and each partial row sum, starting from column 1, is nonnegative.

arxiv-2112-01049.title: Bayesian Optimization over Permutation Spaces
arxiv-2112-01049.creator: Aryan Deshwal, Syrine Belakaria, Janardhan Rao Doppa, Dae Hyun Kim
arxiv-2112-01049.description: Abstract Optimizing expensive to evaluate black-box functions over an input space consisting of all permutations of d d objects is an important problem with many real-world applications. For example, placement of functional blocks in hardware design to optimize performance via simulations. The overall goal is to minimize the number of function evaluations to find high-performing permutations.

arxiv-2201-10426.title: Sequential Parametric Optimization for Rate-Splitting Precoding in Non-Orthogonal Unicast and Multicast Transmissions
arxiv-2201-10426.creator: Luis F. Abanto-Leon 2 , Matthias Hollick 2 , Bruno Clerckx 3 , Gek Hong (Allyson) Sim 2
arxiv-2201-10426.description: Abstract This paper investigates rate-splitting (RS) precoding for non-orthogonal unicast and multicast (NOUM) transmissions using fully-digital and hybrid precoders. We study the nonconvex weighted sum-rate (WSR) maximization problem subject to a multicast requirement. We propose FALCON , an approach based on sequential parametric optimization, to solve the aforementioned problem.

arxiv-2204-00035.title: Curiosity Driven Self-supervised Tactile Exploration of Unknown Objects
arxiv-2204-00035.creator: Jianren Wang Carnegie Mellon University jianrenw@andrew.cmu.edu, Yujie LuUC Santa Barbara yujielu@ucsb.edu Vikash KumarFacebook AI Research vikash@cs.washington.edu
arxiv-2204-00035.description: Abstract Intricate behaviors an organism can exhibit is predicated on its ability to sense and effectively interpret complexities of its surroundings. Relevant information is often distributed between multiple modalities, and requires the organism to exhibit information assimilation capabilities in addition to information seeking behaviors.

arxiv-2206-00860.title: Self-Consistency of the Fokker-Planck Equation
arxiv-2206-00860.creator: Zebang Shen, Zhenfu Wang, Satyen Kale, Alejandro Ribeiro, Amin Karbasi, Hamed Hassani
arxiv-2206-00860.description: Abstract The Fokker-Planck equation (FPE) is the partial differential equation that governs the density evolution of the Itô process and is of great importance to the literature of statistical physics and machine learning. The FPE can be regarded as a continuity equation where the change of the density is completely determined by a time varying velocity field.

arxiv-2206-12320.title: PoCaP Corpus: A Multimodal Dataset for Smart Operating Room Speech Assistant using Interventional Radiology Workflow Analysis Thanks: Seung Hee Yang is the corresponding author.
arxiv-2206-12320.creator: Kubilay Can Demir, Matthias May, Axel Schmid, Michael Uder, Katharina Breininger, Tobias Weise, Andreas Maier, Seung Hee Yang
arxiv-2206-12320.description: Abstract This paper presents a new multimodal interventional radiology dataset, called PoCaP (Port Catheter Placement) Corpus. This corpus consists of speech and audio signals in German, X-ray images, and system commands collected from 31 PoCaP interventions by six surgeons with average duration of 81.4 ± 41.0 81.4\pm 41.0 minutes.

arxiv-2210-00609.title: Throwing Objects into A Moving Basket While Avoiding Obstacles
arxiv-2210-00609.creator: Hamidreza Kasaei, Mohammadreza Kasaei
arxiv-2210-00609.description: Abstract The capabilities of a robot will be increased significantly by exploiting throwing behavior. In particular, throwing will enable robots to rapidly place the object into the target basket, located outside its feasible kinematic space, without traveling to the desired location. In previous approaches, the robot often learned a parameterized throwing kernel through analytical approaches, imitation learning, or hand-coding.

arxiv-2210-04784.title: Physics department, Herzen state Pedagogical University of Russia,
arxiv-2210-04784.creator: 48 Moika Emb., Saint Petersburg 191186, Russia
arxiv-2210-04784.description: Abstract o Extraction Energy From Charged Vaidya Black Hole Via Penrose Process Vitalii Vertogradov Summary . In this paper, we consider the analogy of the Penrose process in Charged Vaidya spacetime. We calculate the border of the generalized ergosphere, in which the charged particles with negative energy might exist, and show that it is temporary.

arxiv-2303-18076.title: Machine learning applications in studies of the physical properties of active galactic nuclei based on photometric observations
arxiv-2303-18076.creator: Sarah Mechbal, Markus Ackermann, Marek Kowalski
arxiv-2303-18076.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Sarah Mechbal, Markus Ackermann, Marek Kowalski. We investigate the physical nature of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) using machine learning (ML) tools. We show that the redshift, z z , bolometric luminosity, L Bol L_{\rm Bol} , central mass of the supermassive black hole (SMBH), M BH M_{\rm BH} , Eddington ratio, λ Edd \lambda_{\rm Edd} , and AGN class (obscured or unobscured) can be reconstructed through multi-wavelength photometric observations only.

arxiv-2305-12353.title: Detection of thermal Sunyaev–Zel’dovich Effect in the circumgalactic medium of low-mass galaxies - a surprising pattern in self-similarity and baryon sufficiency Facilities: WISE, SuperCOSMOS, Planck , Atacama Cosmology Telescope , Jansky Very Large Array AstroPy ( Astropy Collaboration & Astropy Pr
arxiv-2305-12353.creator: Sanskriti Das, Yi-Kuan Chiang, Smita Mathur
arxiv-2305-12353.description: Abstract We report on the measurement of the thermal Sunyaev–Zel’dovich (tSZ) Effect in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) of 641,923 galaxies with M ⋆ \rm M_{\star} = 10 9.8 − 11.3 ​ M ⊙ \rm 10^{9.8-11.3}M_{\odot} at z < z< 0.5, pushing the exploration of tSZ Effect to lower-mass galaxies compared to previous studies.

arxiv-2309-08615.creator: Roblex Nana, Claude Tadonki, Petr Dokladal, Youssef Mesri
arxiv-2309-08615.description: Abstract . For various reasons including those related to climate changes, energy has become a critical concern in all relevant activities and technical designs. For the specific case of computer activities, the problem is exacerbated with the emergence and pervasiveness of the so called intelligent devices .

arxiv-2310-19286.title: Local convergence of a sequential quadratic programming method for a class of nonsmooth nonconvex objectives Thanks: Submitted to the editors.
arxiv-2310-19286.creator: Jingyi Wang, Cosmin G. Petra
arxiv-2310-19286.description: Abstract A sequential quadratic programming (SQP) algorithm is designed for nonsmooth optimization problems with upper- 𝒞 2 \mathcal{C}^{2} objective functions. Upper- 𝒞 2 \mathcal{C}^{2} functions are locally equivalent to difference-of-convex (DC) functions with smooth convex parts. They arise naturally in many applications such as certain classes of solutions to parametric optimization problems, e.g.

arxiv-2406-16249.title: An Optimal Tightness Bound for the Simulation Lemma
arxiv-2406-16249.creator: Sam Lobel, Ronald Parr
arxiv-2406-16249.description: Abstract We present a bound for value-prediction error with respect to model misspecification that is tight, including constant factors. This is a direct improvement of the “simulation lemma,” a foundational result in reinforcement learning. We demonstrate that existing bounds are quite loose, becoming vacuous for large discount factors, due to the suboptimal treatment of compounding probability errors.

arxiv-2504-20391.title: The Mean of Multi-Object Trajectories
arxiv-2504-20391.creator: Tran Thien Dat Nguyen, Ba Tuong Vo, Ba-Ngu Vo, Hoa Van Nguyen, Changbeom Shim
arxiv-2504-20391.description: Abstract This paper introduces the concept of a mean for trajectories and multi-object trajectories (defined as sets or multi-sets of trajectories) along with algorithms for computing them. Specifically, we use the Fréchet mean, and metrics based on the optimal sub-pattern assignment (OSPA) construct, to extend the notion of average from vectors to trajectories and multi-object trajectories.

arxiv-2505-18010.title: Clinical Validation of Deep Learning for Real-Time Tissue Oxygenation Estimation Using Spectral Imaging
arxiv-2505-18010.creator: Jens De Winne, Siri Willems, Siri Luthman, Danilo Babin, Hiep Luong, Wim Ceelen
arxiv-2505-18010.description: Abstract Accurate, real-time monitoring of tissue ischemia is crucial to understand tissue health and guide surgery. Spectral imaging shows great potential for contactless and intraoperative monitoring of tissue oxygenation. Due to the difficulty of obtaining direct reference oxygenation values, conventional methods are based on linear unmixing techniques.

arxiv-2509-00305.title: Language-Aware Information Maximization for Transductive Few-Shot CLIP
arxiv-2509-00305.creator: Ghassen Baklouti ghassen.baklouti.1@ens.etsmtl.ca, Maxime Zanella maxime.zanella@uclouvain.be, Ismail Ben Ayed ismail.benayed@etsmtl.ca
arxiv-2509-00305.description: Abstract Transductive few-shot learning has triggered an abundant literature focusing on vision-only models, but is still at a nascent stage within the recent context of foundational vision-language models (VLMs). Only a few recent methods addressed the problem, pointing to the potential of tranduction in VLMs and to the need for VLM-tailored methods.

arxiv-2509-05023.title: Evaluating Idle Animation Believability: a User Perspective Publication type: Research Article Journal: Journal Volume: 00
arxiv-2509-05023.creator: Eneko Atxa Landa, Elena Lazkano, Igor Rodriguez, Itsaso Rodriguez-Moreno, Itziar Irigoien, Eneko Atxa Landa, Elena Lazkano, Igor Rodriguez, Itsaso Rodríguez-Moreno, Itziar Irigoien
arxiv-2509-05023.description: Abstract Animating realistic avatars requires using high quality animations for every possible state the avatar can be in. This includes actions like walking or running, but also subtle movements that convey emotions and personality. Idle animations, such as standing, breathing or looking around, are crucial for realism and believability.

arxiv-2602-06505.title: Classical Resolution of the Gibbs Paradox from the Equal Probability Principle: An Informational Perspective
arxiv-2602-06505.creator: Zheng Zhang
arxiv-2602-06505.description: Abstract The Gibbs paradox is a conventional paradox in classical statistical mechanics, typically resolved by invoking quantum indistinguishability through the 1 / N ! 1/N! correction. In this letter, we present a resolution within classical ensemble theory, which relies solely on the equal probability principle and does not invoke the 1 / N ! 1/N! correction.

pmc-10539636.creator: L.F. van de Water, S.C. Kuijper, I. Henselmans, E.N. van Alphen, E.S. Kooij, M.M. Calff, L.V. Beerepoot, J. Buijsen, W.J. Eshuis, E.D. Geijsen, S.H.C. Havenith, F.F.B.M. Heesakkers, S. Mook, K. Muller, H.C. Post, H. Rütten, M. Slingerland, T. van Voorthuizen, H.W.M. van Laarhoven, E.M.A. Smets
pmc-10539636.description: SummaryBackgroundFor cancer patients to effectively engage in decision making, they require comprehensive and understandable information regarding treatment options and their associated outcomes. We developed an online prediction tool and supporting communication skills training to assist healthcare providers (HCPs) in this complex task.

pmc-11441112.title: Can Hemogram Parameters and Derived Ratios Predict Conversion From Laparoscopic to Open Cholecystectomy?
pmc-11441112.creator: Mehmet Alperen Avci, Can Akgün, Omer Buk, Dilara Karadan
pmc-11441112.description: BackgroundsLaparoscopic cholecystectomy (LC) is the gold standard for surgical removal of gallbladder today. In challenging cholecystectomy cases, conversion to an open technique may be necessary. Therefore, the preoperative prediction of conversion to open technique holds significant importance for patient safety and surgical strategy. In the literature, conversion to open cholecystectomy has been associated with many contradictory predictive factors.

pmc-11554706.title: Combinations of physical and cognitive training for subcortical neurodegenerative diseases with physical, cognitive and behavioral symptoms: a systematic review
pmc-11554706.creator: Coline Chartier, Julien Godard, Sylvain Durand, Anne Humeau-Heurtier, Emmanuelle Menetrier, Philippe Allain, Jérémy Besnard
pmc-11554706.description: BackgroundThe onset of the symptoms of subcortical NDs is due to a unique part of the brain which strengthens the idea of reciprocal influence of physical activity and cognitive training in improving clinical symptoms. Consequently, protocols combining the two stimulations are becoming increasingly popular in NDs.

pmc-12039817.title: Hydroxyurea reduces the levels of the fetal globin gene repressors ZBTB7A/LRF and BCL11A in erythroid cells in vitro
pmc-12039817.creator: Gabriella E Martyn, Phillip A Doerfler, Yu Yao, Kate G R Quinlan, Mitchell J Weiss, Merlin Crossley
pmc-12039817.description: ObjectivesHydroxyurea (HU) is the most widely used therapy for adults and children with sickle cell disease (SCD). It is believed to act largely by inducing the transcription of fetal γ-globin genes to generate fetal hemoglobin (HbF), which inhibits the pathological polymerization of sickle hemoglobin (HbS). The mechanisms by which hydroxyurea elevates HbF are unclear.

pmc-12596224.title: The Endothelial Glycocalyx: The First Line of Defense in the Prevention and Treatment of Kidney Diseases
pmc-12596224.creator: Xiaoyu Yuan, Mengzhen Jia, Li Zhou, Gailing Hou, Bing Zhang, Xinshou Ouyang, Yanjie Huang
pmc-12596224.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The endothelial glycocalyx (EG) is widely located on the surface of endothelial cell membrane. It serves as an important component of the endothelial cell barrier and plays a crucial role in maintaining charge balance within the cell. The shedding, excessive thickening and deposition of the EG located on the surface of endothelial cells within the renal capillary network is widely observed in acute kidney injury and chronic kidney disease.

pmc-12709802.title: Basophils activate splenic B cells and dendritic cells via IL-13 signaling in acute traumatic brain injury
pmc-12709802.creator: Florian Olde Heuvel, Jin Zhang, Fan Sun, Sruthi Sankari Krishnamurthy, Gizem Yartas, Burak Özkan, Marica Pagliarini, David Voehringer, Caitlin C O’Meara, Michael KE Schäfer, Markus Huber-Lang, Francesco Roselli
pmc-12709802.description: BackgroundPeripheral consequences following traumatic brain injury (TBI) are characterized by both systemic inflammatory responses and autonomic dysregulation. One of the main immune regulatory organs, the spleen, shows high interaction with the brain which is controlled by both circulating mediators as well as autonomic fibers targeting splenic immune cells.

pmc-13034389.title: Integrating cardiovascular healthcare screening into a community pharmacy vaccination service: a scoping review to identify opportunities for patient engagement and service expansion
pmc-13034389.creator: Jason Tang, Gemma Mansell, Piotr Merks, Alison Jones, Jay Badenhorst, Mark Koziol, Daljit Sandhu, Chris Langley
pmc-13034389.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesCommunity pharmacies are increasingly recognised as accessible providers of public health services. Integrating cardiovascular health checks and behaviour change strategies with the community pharmacy vaccination service has the potential to improve population health outcomes.

pmc-13107515.title: Quasi-Operando Liquid-Phase Electron Imaging of Metallic Copper Nanocubes Reveals Step-by-Step Subtle Dissolution, Redeposition, Reattachment, and Fragmentation Mechanisms during CO2 Electroreduction
pmc-13107515.creator: Saltanat Toleukhanova, Petru Albertini, Vasiliki Tileli
pmc-13107515.description: Metallic copper nanocubes used in CO2 electroreduction (CO2ER) are known to exhibit moderate binding energies to intermediates and selectivity toward ethylene. However, the process by which they restructure, ultimately redistributing the active sites and causing deactivation, remains challenging to fully elucidate.

pmc-13429013.title: Clinical cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study of DIAGNOdent Pen and QrayCam Pro quantitative fluorescence for occlusal caries detection and ICDAS II-derived lesion categorization in permanent posterior teeth
pmc-13429013.creator: Ahmad Bittar, Elif Alkan, Dilek Tağtekin
pmc-13429013.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEarly detection of occlusal caries in posterior teeth is important for minimally invasive care. Visual systems such as the International Caries Detection and Assessment System (ICDAS II) standardize clinical scoring, but adjunctive fluorescence-based tools may improve objectivity.
